adaptation.description: The flower has bright pink petals that stand out against green leaves. This colorful coat acts like a bright sign for friendly visitors.
adaptation.imagePrompt: A close-up of a vibrant pink flower with bright pink petals glowing in the sunshine, with green leaves in the background

pressures: Standing out in a sea of green leaves
environment.description: The sunny garden is full of green plants, making it hard for small helpers to find where the sweet treats are hidden.

connection.explanation: The bright pink petals act like a colorful neon sign that tells helpful bugs and birds where to find sweet food. When the helpers visit, they carry pollen to other plants.
evidencePoints: Bright pink color is easy for bees and butterflies to see from far away
Petals guide hungry visitors right to the center of the flower

whatIfScenarios.environmentChange: All the petals turn completely green to match the leaves.
whatIfScenarios.question: Would the green petals still be easy for bees to spot in the garden?
whatIfScenarios.expectedReasoning: No - green petals would blend right into the green leaves, making it much harder for bees to find the flower.

whatIfScenarios.environmentChange: The sun shines even brighter during the day.
whatIfScenarios.question: Would the bright pink petals still help the flower stand out in the bright sun?
whatIfScenarios.expectedReasoning: Yes - bright pink colors still catch the light and look like a colorful sign for visiting bugs.

misconception.commonBelief: Flowers grow bright pink petals just to make the garden pretty for people to look at.
misconception.correction: Flowers actually grow bright petals to attract helpful bugs and birds that help the plant make new seeds.
